Rugged tablet for Prisma Mobile Maintenance (Prisma CMMS)

Prisma is the computerised maintenance management system (CMMS, or GMAO in Spanish) made by Sisteplant, S.L., headquartered in Derio, Spain. Planners and coordinators work in the Prisma web front end, while technicians use the companion app, published on Google Play as Prisma Mobile Maintenance, to receive and report work orders, identify assets and spare parts by QR code, barcode or NFC tag, attach photos and documents, and keep working where there is no signal. Sisteplant lists four sectors for Prisma: services, estate (buildings), infrastructures and industry.

A technician's tablet spends its day on plant floors, in hangars and plant rooms, in the rain and on vehicle dashboards. A consumer tablet usually has no ingress protection rating or drop rating, often has no NFC or SIM slot, and is built for indoor use. Consumer models also change frequently, which is awkward for a fleet that has to be imaged and managed together.

This page sets out what Sisteplant publishes about the devices Prisma Mobile Maintenance runs on, which Tuga tablets meet those published requirements, how to get the app running, and what to think about before a fleet order. One of our customers, an industrial asset-management firm, bought a Tuga A10 for maintenance technicians at an aerospace manufacturer to run this app.

Requirements

What Prisma Mobile Maintenance (Prisma CMMS) needs from a device

Each item below comes from Sisteplant, S.L.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 8.0 or later for the technician app

    The Google Play listing for Prisma Mobile Maintenance (package com.sisteplant.prisma, developer Sisteplant) states that the app requires Android 8.0 and up. The current version at the time of checking was 13.0.6, updated on 6 May 2026. Sisteplant also publishes an iOS and iPadOS app under the different name Prisma Mobile, which requires iOS 11.0 or iPadOS 11.0 or later. Source: play.google.com

  • A Prisma server the app can connect to

    The app is a front end to a Prisma installation. The App Store listing states a server at Prisma 3 V8.2.1.166 or later is needed, and Sisteplant's Prisma 4 release bulletin says the store versions of the apps are compatible with all Prisma 4 sub-versions. The bulletin also states that an SSL (https) installation is required for downloading the apps and for web camera access. Source: apps.apple.com

  • Offline working for work-order reporting, with some functions online only

    Google Play describes Prisma Mobile as a multi-device app that can be used both online and offline, allowing it to be used in areas with no signal. It lists online and offline work-order reports covering labour, external material, warehouse articles with readable labels, preventive and predictive maintenance rules, defects, causes and actions, load, texts, images and digital signature. The same listing marks access to the asset hierarchy and start and end labour time logging as online functions. The Prisma 4 bulletin adds that offline login works only with the last credentials used. Source: play.google.com

  • QR code and barcode reading through the device camera

    Google Play lists direct access to a work order or an asset by QR code or barcode reading, and warehouse articles with readable labels. Sisteplant's training page describes identifying assets, work orders and spare parts with the camera of your phone or tablet. No dedicated scan engine is specified by the vendor. Source: sisteplant.com

  • NFC for asset and spare-part identification

    Sisteplant's training page carries the heading identification by barcode, QR or NFC for assets, work orders and spare parts, and a Sisteplant webinar page repeats that assets, work orders and spare parts can be identified with barcodes, QR or NFC. RFID is not mentioned in any vendor source we found, so we do not claim RFID support. Source: sisteplant.com

  • Microsoft Edge or Chrome for the Prisma web front end on Windows

    The Prisma 4 release bulletin states that browsing with Internet Explorer is not possible from release 12 onwards and names Microsoft Edge and Chrome as the supported browsers. The technician app is published only on Google Play and the Apple App Store; we found no Windows build or Microsoft Store listing, so on a Windows device the relevant software is the web front end used by planners and coordinators. Source: sisteplant.com

  • No published device models or screen-size guidance

    Sisteplant does not publish recommended tablet models, hardware specifications or screen-size guidance. Google Play calls Prisma Mobile a multi-device app for mobile devices, and the vendor's training page refers to using the camera of your phone or tablet. Device choice is therefore down to the buyer, within the Android 8.0 or later requirement. Source: play.google.com

Worth knowing. The technician app, Prisma Mobile Maintenance, is published for Android (Google Play) and for iOS and iPadOS under the name Prisma Mobile (App Store). We found no native Windows build or Microsoft Store listing, so the Tuga W10 can only run the Prisma web front end in Edge or Chrome for planners and coordinators, not the technician app. The Tuga A10 has no dedicated scan engine; QR and barcode reading is through the camera and is handled by the app, which is also how Sisteplant describes it, but if your site has a hard requirement for a hardware scanner the A10 does not provide one. Setting up

Getting Prisma Mobile Maintenance (Prisma CMMS) running

  1. Confirm with your Prisma administrator or Sisteplant that your server version supports the current app (the App Store listing states Prisma 3 V8.2.1.166 or later, and Sisteplant says the store apps are compatible with all Prisma 4 sub-versions) and that it is reachable over https, which the Prisma 4 bulletin says is required for app downloads and camera access.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, sign in to a Google account (a managed account from your mobile device management system if you use one), open Google Play and install Prisma Mobile Maintenance by Sisteplant.
  3. Open the app and sign in with the server details and user credentials your Prisma administrator provides. Do the first sign-in with a connection, because the vendor states offline login works only with the last credentials used on the device.
  4. Let the app download its master data on first connection, then test a QR code or barcode scan and an NFC tag read on a real asset label before rolling out to the team.
  5. Check an offline cycle: put the tablet in flight mode, report a work order, reconnect and confirm it syncs. Remember that Sisteplant lists asset hierarchy access and start and end labour time logging as online functions.
  6. For the Prisma web front end on a Tuga W10, open Microsoft Edge, browse to your Prisma https address and sign in. On any model, fit a screen protector and add a vehicle mounting dock or charging dock before the devices go out.
